chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Hanan ibn Sadir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him: Do people of two different religions inherit from each other? He said: 'No.'
ai.seo_question: Do Muslims and non-Muslims inherit from each other in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the principle of *al-muwatana bi'l-millatayn* (co-religionality) in inheritance, ruling that individuals of different faiths do not inherit from each other. This establishes a foundational legal distinction in Shia jurisprudence, emphasizing that the bond of faith supersedes kinship for the purpose of inheriting wealth, a ruling derived from the Quranic verse 'And you are allies of one another.'
